stories.summary: Training coding agents typically updates the policy while keeping the harness fixed. For flawed repair strategies, a frozen teacher generates task-specific mechanism-level skills. stories.whyNow: Introduces co-adaptation of execution harnesses alongside policy weights during RL training.

stories.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. items.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
items.summary: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator. Existing state quantizers round the state after every generated token and report that four bits lose accuracy unless the bit width is raised or the model is fine-tuned.\par We introduce PACE, a post-hoc four-bit state quantizer. PACE rounds the state only once every few generated tokens, as chunked kernels already do…

items.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources. Conventional dense multi-view reconstruction methods can produce high-quality volumetric videos, but their reliance on costly capture setups makes them impractical in real-world scenarios. Recent approaches use generative models to relax capture requirements, but still suffer from limited resolution and 4D inconsistency. To overcome these constraints, we propose RealMe, a unified framework built around a high-resolution video diffusion model that enhances limited captures…

items.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
items.summary: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outra…

items.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
items.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. We introduce Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed for measuring how far today's agents can improve the published best models on scientific ML benchmarks, spanning 20 benchmarks across 11 domains. Rather than ranking agents on a leaderboard, Agent4Sci asks what kinds of progress agents can make on these tasks under in-the-wild conditions, and where they fall short. E…

items.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
items.summary: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the…

items.summary: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. items.title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
items.summary: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. items.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
items.summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. items.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
items.summary: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associa…

items.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
items.summary: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. items.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. items.summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. items.title: Agentic World Action Models
items.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. items.summary: As LLMs expand their language coverage, evaluating how well they understand and represent diverse cultures becomes increasingly important. However, many benchmarks remain English-centric, with limited cultural coverage and a focus on factual knowledge over its application in real-world cultural contexts. We propose CulturalRiddles, a benchmark of original, culturally grounded riddles created entirely by humans through a participatory community effort, spanning 62 cultures (45 countries, 51 languages). items.summary: Aiming to modify textual content while preserving the original style, Scene Text Editing (STE) has significant practical value in many applications. STE typically requires paired images before and after editing for training. However, recent approaches rely heavily on synthetic paired data and complex disentanglement strategies. items.summary: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. items.summary: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks. items.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. items.summary: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. items.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
items.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. items.title: RubatoCodec: Budgeted Adaptive Speech Tokenization with Streaming Decoding
items.summary: Neural speech codecs provide discrete tokens for speech generation. Lower frame rates shorten token sequences, but each token must then carry more linguistic and acoustic information. Variable-frame-rate codecs address this trade-off by adapting token allocation to speech content, but threshold-based allocation lets content determine the token count, so the sequence length a speech generator must produce varies across utterances and datasets at a fixed setting. items.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
items.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. items.summary: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. items.summary: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer. items.summary: A fine-tuned Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy can easily place the alphabet soup in the basket on command, just as it saw during fine-tuning. items.summary: Real-world observations are noisy and often contain excessive task-irrelevant information. items.summary: Google has joined Amazon in releasing a developer tool that makes it easy for PyTorch users to move their apps off Nvidia GPUs.

items.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
items.summary: The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.

items.title: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
items.summary: Electric Plant has built an AI-powered translator to help humans listen to what plants are saying with the subtle electricity coursing through their stems.

items.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
items.summary:
A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI.
New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand - with gas turbines or renewable energy - will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim.
Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all…
items.author: Justine Calma

items.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
items.summary:
Meta says it's issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
"The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant," Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new clas…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
items.summary:
Anthropic just announced an AI agent competitor to Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots: Claude Duet. The new agent, designed for professionals and small business owners, is launching as a "research preview," according to Anthropic, and it's available as a standalone app on iOS and Android and through Claude on the web.
The AI agent is built around Claude Opus 5.5. Here's Anthropic's description of what it can do:
Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs…
items.author: Jay Peters

items.title: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you
items.summary:
Walmart will soon let AI agents shop on its website for you. Next month, the retail giant will allow you to use an AI agent on the site, with systems in place to let you approve and review purchases and set spending limits.
The embrace of AI agents stands in stark contrast to Amazon, which blocked Perplexity's shopping agent and Meta's Muse AI assistant. But Walmart is opening its doors to AI shoppers - as long as they follow the retailer's rules. It has outlined a set of terms for agents, saying that "agents must not take actions beyond what the shopper intends" and cannot change a customer'…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
items.summary:
After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with "rollout happening globally too," according to Google (we've asked for specific regional availability details).
It's taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. That includes asking it multi-step questions, such as recommendations on places to visit and then prompting it to…
items.author: Jess Weatherbed

items.title: OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
items.summary:
OpenAI disclosed a pair of safety incidents that involved AI agents weakening their safety monitoring systems during internal coding tasks. In one incident, OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra agent disabled its safety monitor when copying reference code - and then lied about it.
"The reference didn't configure a monitor, and Astra decided that was reason to remove the monitoring integration from the user's code," Marcus Williams, an AI safety researcher at OpenAI, writes on X. "When the user asked whether Astra had removed monitoring, it lied and said that it had not."
A separate incident occurred a…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
items.summary:
On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.
When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, "Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about o…
items.author: Richard Lawler

items.title: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
items.summary:
Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search.
As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you're driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. You can also ask Gemini to "take me to my doctor's appointment" instead of pulling up directions manually, o…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web
items.summary:
Meta says it paused a Muse feature that lets you share conversations with the AI assistant after researchers found the URLs publicly available on the web, as reported by Ars Technica. In a report published this week, researchers at the security firm Claroc say they found more than 6,800 Muse links through public DNS records.
"People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link," Muse spokesperson Tracy Clayton says in an emailed statement to The Verge. "However, we've paused this functionality while we review this report a…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
items.summary:
Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year. That's according to an announcement on Tuesday that says Spotify has also made changes to its recommendation system to highlight more music made by human artists.
"Our editors hold the same standard and don't program content identified as slop or spam," Spotify says. "Since we made these changes, we've seen a marked decrease in listener concerns about this content showing up in recommendations."
Though Spotify has stopped short of mandating labels on all AI…
items.author: Emma Roth

items.title: Agentic World Action Models
items.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this archite…
items.author: Zhuoyang Liu

items.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods targe…
items.author: Zhennan Wan

items.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
items.summary: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model s…
items.author: Adrien Ramanana Rahary

items.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
items.summary: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outra…
items.author: Zhanshuo Cao

items.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
items.summary: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program…
items.author: Zhichao Zhai

items.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
items.summary: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without…
items.author: Yunhao Luo

items.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
items.summary: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.
items.author: Ashkan Soleymani

items.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
items.summary: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. However, existing encoders typically specialize in only one or two of these capabilities; we therefore introduce ALPS, a pretrained visual state encoder that unifies all three in a single set of patch tokens. Using only still images and text, we pretrain a ViT-B/16 from scratch with language, reconstruction,…
items.author: Yanqing Liu

items.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
items.summary: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of…
items.author: Imon Banerjee

items.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
items.summary: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in…
items.author: Francesco Mori

items.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
items.summary: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predi…
items.author: Houzhu Ding

items.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
items.summary: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. Each model writes environments, each with a privileged hint, aiming for tasks that capable solvers fail without the hint and pass with it. Across nine frontier LLMs, solving and authoring prove to be distinct…
items.author: Shibo Jin

items.title: The End of Consensus Research?
items.summary: Consensus is a fundamental problem in distributed computing and at the core of state machine replication (SMR). Despite decades of active human research, discovering practical low-latency solutions to the problem is still open, as it requires combining protocol knowledge, correctness reasoning, implementation, and experimental evaluation. We report on how AI helped us discover A-greement, a new consensus protocol for geo-replicated state machines that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions. Averaged across six deployments with 5 or 9 replicas, A-greement reduces the mean latency…
items.author: Clément Burgelin

items.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
items.summary: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data. A model constructs features and stock-scoring code, receives feedback only on 2022…
items.author: Houde Qian

items.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
items.summary: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consis…
items.author: Shayan Hundrieser

items.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
items.summary: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the…
items.author: Yanzhe Chen

items.title: Velocity Ambiguity Profiles: Time-Resolved Bayes-Risk Diagnostics for Flow Matching
items.summary: Flow matching trains a continuum of velocity regression problems but usually reports a loss averaged over interpolation time, obscuring which regions are limited by intrinsic ambiguity and which remain data-limited. We introduce the Velocity Ambiguity Profile (VAP), $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$, the time-local Bayes-risk floor of velocity prediction, and decompose time-resolved loss as $L_N(t)=\mathcal{A}_v(t)+R(t;N)$, where only the excess term $R(t;N)$ is reducible by more data or a different estimator. For $N$ training samples and a $K$-component mixture in the structured example, we prove two stati…
items.author: Yunpeng Mei

items.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
items.summary: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that…
items.author: Sriyash Poddar

items.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
items.summary: Despite recent advances, current AI systems remain highly susceptible to domain shifts, particularly in biomedical imaging, where images are usually acquired under substantially different experimental conditions. Although recent domain adaptation methods have made substantial progress, significant performance gaps under domain shift persist. To measure progress in this regard, we introduce BatchBench, a leaderboard that evaluates and compares the robustness of AI systems on biomedical images from unseen experimental batches and data sources. BatchBench is built on JUMP-CP, one of the largest…
items.author: Sonja Topf

items.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
items.summary: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. A model that reasons rather than recalls should notice which side of this boundary a problem falls on, yet existing benchmarks either fix the wording of each task or ignore its complexity class, so they cannot separate the two. We introduce P2NPCBench, a benchmark of 12 problem families in which every NPC problem is paired with a P twin posed over the same surface. To remove the textbook cues that enable recall, we build it with AgentGAN, an advers…
items.author: Nurul Labib Sayeedi

items.title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network
items.summary: This report describes a laboratory instantiation of a dynamic microsegmentation function for an Internet-of-Things network, specifically a multi-robot network, using a commercial software-defined microsegmentation tool. Fine-grained dynamic segmentation policies are defined, where segments are adapted based on asset functional and health tags. Automated implementation of the dynamic policies in software is also undertaken. The microsegmentation solution is shown to automatically isolate an indicated threat in real time, while maintaining unaffected operations. The demonstration indicates that…
items.author: Vishwam Raval

items.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) has become a central paradigm for aligning Large Language Models with human values. However, the reliance on sensitive preference data necessitates rigorous differential privacy (DP) guarantees to prevent user information leakage. Existing private alignment methods typically assume dense reward parameterizations, resulting in estimation error bounds that scale polynomially with the ambient {model size $d$}. Such dependence is prohibitive in modern {overparameterized models} where $d$ is vast. In this work, we study \emph{Private Sparse RLHF} p…
items.author: Meng Ding

items.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for…
items.author: Likui Zhang

items.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
items.summary: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. In late 2026 a class of commercial System One decision models (TypeSafe Jev; Microsoft-Decision-1) began selling typed decision primitives - binary gates, closed-set choices, ordinal scores - as product APIs, with no academic treatment. We present VX-One: a small multi-head network (100K-10M parameters) whose outputs are these primitives - a calibrated gate, a choice over a closed candidate s…
items.author: Juan S. Santillana

items.title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
items.summary: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. Doing so on the user's behalf requires identifying what matters, understanding the scene in real time, and initiating memory maintenance in the background while the user stays focused on their activities. We introduce ProactEgoMem, a benchmark that evaluates proactive memory in streaming egocentric video. T…
items.author: Ruotong Liao

items.title: Orbitol: Crystal Generation on Wyckoff Orbits
items.summary: Generative models propose crystalline materials by learning composition and geometry, but unconditional sampling gives no direct control over the space group, which constrains whether responses such as piezoelectricity are symmetry-allowed. We present Orbitol, a crystal generator built on the Crystalite diffusion Transformer that replaces atom tokens with Wyckoff-orbit tokens. Given a space group and a collection of occupied Wyckoff positions, Orbitol generates the atom type and free coordinates of each orbit together with a compatible lattice, so every valid structure is invariant under the…
items.author: Ivan Žugec

items.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
items.summary: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. Learned locomotion has studied reduced gravity on rigid ground and granular terrain mostly at Earth gravity, but not humanoids under both, generalist-controller transfer, or the Earth cost of lunar adaptation. On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity…
items.author: Guillem Casadesus Vila

items.title: Circuits of LLM Classifiers
items.summary: Language models make it easy to build classifiers by simply prompting a model with the sample to classify. However, their predictions are neither deterministic nor uniformly reliable across samples. How can we combine predictions from different models to improve reliability? We view LLM classifiers as noisy measurement instruments of an underlying target label. Our goal is to maximize average classification accuracy at a given average query cost. To this end, we introduce circuits that organize LLM classifiers into an adaptive sequence of queries and decisions. We then characterize the optima…
items.author: Hadi Khalaf

items.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
items.summary: Personalized federated learning must decide which clients should share representations. We introduce HDC-FL (Head-Derived Clustering for Personalized Federated Learning), which reads that decision off a signal shared-encoder training already produces: the client-specific classifi- er heads. At periodic refresh rounds the server projects the cached heads into a normalized low-rank descriptor space, groups the descriptors, builds one encoder prototype per group from the cached client encoders, and returns to each client a soft mixture of those prototypes paired with its own unchanged head. Clie…
items.author: Amirardalan Dehghanpour

items.title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
items.summary: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/χ_f(G)$ fraction of the to…
items.author: Hanmin Li

items.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
items.summary: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. We first build \probe{}, a suite of 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions, and find a persistent gap between what a…
items.author: Xinzhe Wang

items.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
items.summary: Recent Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) use Self-Conditioning (SC), or Loopholing, to improve their performance. While SC is traditionally seen as an auxiliary heuristic, its empirical success raises the question: can a continuous generative model be based purely on Self-Conditioning? We answer affirmatively with LAW (``Loopholing All the Way''), which propagates the Expected Embedding under the denoiser's prediction across steps, decoding the tokens once, at the end. On Sudoku, LAW outperforms previous Discrete and Continuous Diffusion Models, including Loopholing Discrete Diffusion. On Maze…
items.author: Adrien Deschenaux

items.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
items.summary: Vietnamese pre-trained encoders have improved rapidly, but the strongest ones are large, multilingual-vocabulary models or depend on external word segmentation, which makes them costly to deploy. We present GoiBERT, a family of two compact Vietnamese encoders with 26M and 49M parameters that operate directly on raw text. GoiBERT learns from two complementary teachers. A same-tokenizer Vietnamese encoder first teaches general-purpose representations. A much larger teacher then provides task-level guidance through soft labels that are generated without ever labeling its own training data. Acros…
items.author: Quang Anh Kiet Tran

items.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance. Recently, selective looping, which recursively applies a few early Transformer layers within each denoising…
items.author: Saiteja Utpala

items.title: Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery
items.summary: Humanoid fall recovery requires selecting a motion that suits both the surrounding scene and the task. The same fallen pose can admit several ways to stand, with different routes, support transitions, and final headings. Yet reliable recovery alone does not provide control over which of these alternatives the robot executes. Steering this choice requires anticipating the physical consequences of a requested movement. We present RISE, an approach to perceptive humanoid recovery that lets task objectives steer how the robot returns to standing at inference time. It builds on two insights: diver…
items.author: Osher Azulay

items.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
items.summary: Recent advances in frontier AI models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, planning, and tool use, raising the possibility of using general-purpose AI models for robot manipulation without task-specific training. However, their manipulation capabilities have not been systematically evaluated on standardized robotics benchmarks. In this report, we present a unified closed-loop manipulation framework for evaluating frontier AI models on the LIBERO-10 benchmark. Our framework enables models to control a robot directly through visual observations, robot pr…
items.author: May Espinola

items.title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
items.summary: Coding agents are typically evaluated using one-shot, well-formulated prompts. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench use existing GitHub issues as input for a coding agent and evaluate whether the agent successfully solves the task. However, in real-world use cases, prompts are often not as well-formulated or structured as existing GitHub issues. Additionally, a coding agent session is not limited to a single prompt; it typically involves a multi-turn interaction in which the user iteratively adds new tasks and requirements that the agent must fulfill. To benchmark these abilities, we developed SWE-DI…
items.author: Lorenz Brehme

items.title: Which Differences Matter? Controlled Tests of Rule Transfer, Joint Reliability, and Information Use in Decision Models
items.summary: Decision models map stated rules and observed states to discrete answers. Aggregate accuracy leaves unresolved which rule and information changes guide those answers. We connect controlled input changes to transfer, joint reliability, and directed information use through executable arithmetic rules. Semantic rule separation and crossed rule and state tests make transfer and joint success separately measurable. items.summary: Empirical exchange-correlation functionals are fitted on fixed orbitals but used self-consistently, so better energies often come with worse densities. Penalizing it requires no self-consistent-field solution during training. Trained on 6 energies and 11 CCSD densities, a neural meta-GGA surpasses SCAN in both atomization energies and densities of unseen molecules.

items.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
items.summary:
Sometimes, giving an AI agent all of the knowledge it needs is the wrong approach. At Meta, we’ve seen notable improvements in efficiency and accuracy by keeping the orchestration layer of our data pipeline agents deliberately thin: It routes work and enforces reliability checks, while specialized agents do the domain reasoning. We’re sharing our own [...]

## The data bottleneck in physical AI

High-density demonstration data currently sets the upper limit on physical AI capabilities. Gathering clean robot trajectories via human teleoperation remains expensive, typically costing $10 to $50 per trajectory when accounting for hardware wear, setup time, and operator labor. Scaling physical teleoperation to cover millions of long-tail corner cases—such as unexpected object slippage, dynamic occlusions, or extreme lighting conditions—presents a severe cost bottleneck for robotics engineering teams.

Teams traditionally rely on physics engines like NVIDIA Isaac Sim to procedurally generate synthetic training data. While ray-traced simulation provides ground-truth kinematics, manually constructing CAD assets, tuning contact materials, and configuring scene graphs creates a severe asset bottleneck. This limits how quickly developers can synthesize diverse, long-tail environments.

Generative world models offer an alternative paradigm by replacing manual physics asset creation with neural scene generation. By shifting physical simulation into an asset-free, promptable video generation framework, robotics teams can synthesize multi-view trajectory data directly from latent representations. To accelerate this transition, the [NVIDIA Cosmos platform](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cosmos-open-train-evaluate-deploy-world-models) has expanded to provide data blueprints and checkpoints that rank on six different open models leaderboards.

## Cosmos architectural mechanics

The Cosmos platform uses a dual-track generative architecture to balance spatial consistency with action conditioning. Continuous diffusion models handle visual realism and spatial detail across multi-view camera outputs. Complementing continuous diffusion, discrete tokenizers convert visual frames and physical controls into discrete latent tokens. This discrete representation enables autoregressive next-frame prediction conditioned directly on robot action inputs.

To process raw video data at scale, the pipeline integrates the Cosmos Data Factory. This architecture includes Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets that now supports multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Cosmos Curator filters raw video streams, extracts structured captions, and aligns multi-sensor visual feeds into standardized datasets suitable for domain-specific fine-tuning.

Action conditioning interfaces allow developers to inject continuous robotic states directly into the generative layers. Proprioceptive state vectors, end-effector trajectories, and joint velocities are introduced into latent spatio-temporal layers. This structure ensures that visual frame updates correspond directly to specific motor commands rather than unconditioned visual drifts.

Industrial teams are leveraging this architecture to accelerate development workflows:

* **Automotive simulation:** Porsche uses Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%.
* **Legged robotics:** ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips using Cosmos Data Factory blueprints and validated the outputs using Encord's platform.
* **Reasoning and distillation:** MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on human manipulation videos and distilled a 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model without losing accuracy.
* **Inference optimization:** Updated [NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cosmos-open-train-evaluate-deploy-world-models) deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations.

## Tooling and workflow upgrades

NVIDIA expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints, and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. These releases streamline domain adaptation, allowing teams to fine-tune world models on proprietary hardware platforms without building custom dataset ingestion pipelines from scratch.

The Cosmos Data Factory offers five cloud-native blueprints available through GitHub, Microsoft Azure, Nebius, and CoreWeave:

* **Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation:** Synthesizes multi-camera driving sequences across edge cases and rare weather configurations.
* **Image Attribute Augmentation:** Alters environmental parameters such as lighting, surface reflectivity, and object textures across existing dataset frames.
* **Event Video Generation:** Produces temporally consistent video sequences tailored for dynamic event-based sensor simulation.
* **Defect Image Generation:** Generates structural anomalies and surface defects for industrial inspection and quality control workflows.
* **Video Data Augmentation:** Applies motion-consistent spatial and temporal augmentations to increase effective training corpus scale.

These blueprints provide standardized recipes for scaling training data pipelines across distributed GPU infrastructure. Compared to standard diffusion models trained on unstructured web data, Cosmos simulation checkpoints demonstrate higher sample efficiency when fine-tuned on physical interaction datasets. This sample efficiency enables domain adaptation with significantly fewer hardware trajectory hours.

Across standardized benchmarks, the platform demonstrates state-of-the-art capability. The NVIDIA Cosmos platform ranks in the top five on six different open models leaderboards, providing a validated foundation for synthetic trajectory generation.

## Where synthetic rollouts break down

Despite structural improvements, generative world models introduce physical consistency failure modes that do not occur in classical physics engines. Builders deploying world models into policy training pipelines must monitor three main breakdown points:

* **Non-physical hallucinations:** Neural video generation prioritizes pixel-level perceptual quality over physical invariants. Under complex manipulation tasks, models frequently produce object interpenetration, disappearing contact points, and mass conservation violations. A simulated parallel gripper might appear to pass through a rigid object's geometry instead of imparting normal contact forces.
* **Inference latency bottlenecks:** Generating offline video batches for behavior cloning is computationally straightforward. However, evaluating world models online inside Model Predictive Control (MPC) loops demands immediate frame generation. Even with Cosmos 3 NIM microservices delivering up to 2x faster inference, multi-step autoregressive rollouts across long horizons introduce latency that limits real-time closed-loop control.
* **Sim-to-real visual reality gap:** Fine-tuning policy networks directly on synthetic visual rollouts can cause models to fit to latent generative artifacts. If a policy network learns to exploit visual generation anomalies rather than physical state cues, downstream zero-shot transfer onto physical hardware degrades.

Understanding these failure modes allows teams to design verification layers that prevent unphysical synthetic frames from corrupting downstream policy training.

## What to build and evaluate next

To integrate Cosmos effectively into a robotics data pipeline, builders should adopt a staged evaluation and verification architecture:

1. **Conduct isolated task benchmarks:** Evaluate Cosmos simulation checkpoints directly against traditional Isaac Sim ray-traced data on specific manipulation primitives, such as rigid-body assembly or flexible cable manipulation. Quantify how many synthetic rollouts are required to reach target policy success rates compared to pure physical or physics-simulated datasets.
2. **Implement automated verification pipelines:** Deploy closed-loop verification layers to filter out non-physical trajectories before they enter policy training buffers. Use pose estimation frameworks like FoundationPose or deterministic edge-detection filters to measure geometric persistence and automatically prune frames where objects interpenetrate or disappear.
3. **Deploy hybrid planning topologies:** Combine fast Cosmos autoregressive discrete representations for long-horizon semantic task planning with deterministic physics engines or low-level controller execution. Using the world model primarily for high-level state progression mitigates low-level contact inconsistencies while preserving semantic generalization.

For simulation deployment, Cosmos 3 Nano model variants enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. When serving these models in production, deploy using updated Cosmos 3 NIM microservices to leverage the 2x inference speedups across host clusters.

**Next Steps for Builders:** Clone the cloud-native blueprints on GitHub or Microsoft Azure, set up an automated filtering pipeline using FoundationPose, and benchmark fine-tuned Cosmos checkpoints against your team's baseline Isaac Sim datasets on long-tail manipulation scenarios.

* **Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation:** Synthesizes multi-camera driving sequences across edge cases and rare weather configurations.
* **Image Attribute Augmentation:** Alters environmental parameters such as lighting, surface reflectivity, and object textures across existing dataset frames.
* **Event Video Generation:** Produces temporally consistent video sequences tailored for dynamic event-based sensor simulation.
* **Defect Image Generation:** Generates structural anomalies and surface defects for industrial inspection and quality control workflows.
* **Video Data Augmentation:** Applies motion-consistent spatial and temporal augmentations to increase effective training corpus scale.

These blueprints provide standardized recipes for scaling training data pipelines across distributed GPU infrastructure. Compared to standard diffusion models trained on unstructured web data, Cosmos simulation checkpoints demonstrate higher sample efficiency when fine-tuned on physical interaction datasets. This sample efficiency enables domain adaptation with significantly fewer hardware trajectory hours.

Across standardized benchmarks, the platform demonstrates state-of-the-art capability. The NVIDIA Cosmos platform ranks in the top five on six different open models leaderboards, providing a validated foundation for synthetic trajectory generation.

## Where synthetic rollouts break down

Despite structural improvements, generative world models introduce physical consistency failure modes that do not occur in classical physics engines. Builders deploying world models into policy training pipelines must monitor three main breakdown points:

* **Non-physical hallucinations:** Neural video generation prioritizes pixel-level perceptual quality over physical invariants. Under complex manipulation tasks, models frequently produce object interpenetration, disappearing contact points, and mass conservation violations. A simulated parallel gripper might appear to pass through a rigid object's geometry instead of imparting normal contact forces.
* **Inference latency bottlenecks:** Generating offline video batches for behavior cloning is computationally straightforward. However, evaluating world models online inside Model Predictive Control (MPC) loops demands immediate frame generation. Even with Cosmos 3 NIM microservices delivering up to 2x faster inference, multi-step autoregressive rollouts across long horizons introduce latency that limits real-time closed-loop control.
* **Sim-to-real visual reality gap:** Fine-tuning policy networks directly on synthetic visual rollouts can cause models to fit to latent generative artifacts. If a policy network learns to exploit visual generation anomalies rather than physical state cues, downstream zero-shot transfer onto physical hardware degrades.

Understanding these failure modes allows teams to design verification layers that prevent unphysical synthetic frames from corrupting downstream policy training.

## What to build and evaluate next

To integrate Cosmos effectively into a robotics data pipeline, builders should adopt a staged evaluation and verification architecture:

1. **Conduct isolated task benchmarks:** Evaluate Cosmos simulation checkpoints directly against traditional Isaac Sim ray-traced data on specific manipulation primitives, such as rigid-body assembly or flexible cable manipulation. Quantify how many synthetic rollouts are required to reach target policy success rates compared to pure physical or physics-simulated datasets.
2. **Implement automated verification pipelines:** Deploy closed-loop verification layers to filter out non-physical trajectories before they enter policy training buffers. Use pose estimation frameworks like FoundationPose or deterministic edge-detection filters to measure geometric persistence and automatically prune frames where objects interpenetrate or disappear.
3. **Deploy hybrid planning topologies:** Combine fast Cosmos autoregressive discrete representations for long-horizon semantic task planning with deterministic physics engines or low-level controller execution. Using the world model primarily for high-level state progression mitigates low-level contact inconsistencies while preserving semantic generalization.

For simulation deployment, Cosmos 3 Nano model variants enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. When serving these models in production, deploy using updated Cosmos 3 NIM microservices to leverage the 2x inference speedups across host clusters.

**Next Steps for Builders:** Clone the cloud-native blueprints on GitHub or Microsoft Azure, set up an automated filtering pipeline using FoundationPose, and benchmark fine-tuned Cosmos checkpoints against your team's baseline Isaac Sim datasets on long-tail manipulation scenarios.

Google used its expo slot to present an end-to-end AI Scientist, complete with a sub-agent that checks a claim's novelty against the historical literature and another that generates the paper's figures. A workshop spent a full day debating whether these systems are tools, co-authors, or founders. pastPosts.title: Identity for Reasoning Agents: A Research Brief
pastPosts.summary: Blog Post ← Back to Home Security Identity for Reasoning Agents: A Research Brief Jessica Chen June 25, 2026 CONTENTS Heading Sub-heading A service account does the same thing forever, so a static, broadly scoped credential mostly works for it. An AI agent does not. It reasons, and what it needs access to changes mid-task as it interprets results and decides what to do next. A coding agent starts with read access to a repository, decides it should run the test suite, then deploy, then read a production database to debug a failing test — an escalation chain no static grant anticipated. That gap, between a credential issued once and an actor whose needs evolve as it thinks, is what this event is about. Agents are a new class of actor: they hold credentials like a machine but act with the autonomy of a user, and they are multiplying inside systems never designed to govern them. The hard problem of agent engineering is no longer capability. In production the dominant risk is not that the model says something wrong; it is that a capable agent holding standing, over-scoped credentials does something wrong, and the blast radius is whatever those credentials could reach. pastPosts.summary: Blog Post ← Back to Home AI x Science AI for Life Sciences: Takeaways from the Salon Nina Liu May 28, 2026 CONTENTS Heading Sub-heading #1: "The Most Underrated Unlock for Working Scientists Isn't a New Model — It's a Coding Agent" Nobody came to this dinner to talk about coding agents. The conversation went there anyway. The emerging consensus: the most immediate and underrated unlock for AI in science right now is coding agents, not larger models or better architectures. The reason is structural. Scientific work — prediction models, survival analysis, omics pipelines, multi-parameter optimization — ultimately reduces to code. # AGI House Research Blog: Style Guide

### Voice and Tone
Concrete, rigorous, and technical. Write builder-to-builder. Treat the audience as peer engineers: prioritize architecture, benchmarks, and systems-level tradeoffs over speculative excitement. Zero hype.

### Openings
Open with why this matters *now* in one or two sentences. Establish the stakes immediately by contrasting past constraints with current capabilities, or by framing the commercial and engineering bottleneck currently breaking open.

### Structure and Headings
* **Paragraphs:** Keep them short (2–4 sentences).
* **Headings:** Use plain, direct words (e.g., "Paranoia as method") rather than clever phrasing.
* **Comparisons:** Use bulleted lists to break down model specs, release timelines, or technical comparisons.

### Sources, Names, and Numbers
* **Attribution:** Name the specific labs, papers, models, and people. Link to primary sources inline.
* **Precision:** Ground claims in concrete data—dates, latencies, compute horizons, or benchmark metrics.
* **Quotes:** Keep direct quotes under 15 words and always attribute them to a specific person.

### Closings and Community
Close with immediate utility: tell the reader what to build, read, or watch next (linking talk recordings or papers). When honest and relevant, tie the topic directly to AGI House hackathons, summits, or resident builders.

### Three Things to Avoid
1. **Unsubstantiated hype:** Avoid breathless adjectives ("revolutionary," "mind-blowing"); report the architectural shifts and raw metrics instead.
2. **Long quotes:** Avoid block quotes. Distill the takeaway and keep any quoted phrase under 15 words.
3. **Forced promo:** Do not insert artificial AGI House plugs if the piece does not originate from or tie cleanly to a community event or builder.
